outcome.shown: A bicycle stays upright primarily through a combination of forward motion, gyroscopic effects, and the unique steering geometry designed into the front fork (known as trail). As the bike begins to lean, the front wheel naturally steers slightly into the direction of the fall due to gravity and this trail effect, shifting the wheels back underneath the bike's center of mass and allowing the rider to easily correct their balance.
